function: no_learning: the DNN only approximates the pixel-RIS element response (p. 6); channel estimation is model-based LS (p. 6-8) and beamforming is a relaxation solved with Adam per instance (p. 10)
notes: Excluded as no_learning (borderline call, flagged for the reviewer). The only learned element is a DNN, with a Legendre-kernel alternative, that approximates the 4D response of one pixel-RIS element; it is trained by supervised NMSE regression on 10^7 angle pairs per state (p. 6: "train the weights" ... "to minimize the approximation NMSE"). It models RIS hardware and is independent of the propagation (p. 4: "determined solely by the structure of the pixel RIS element"). The physical-layer functions are not learned. Section IV is "MODEL-BASED CHANNEL ESTIMATION" (p. 6), an LS and grid-search procedure (Algorithm 1 on p. 8, Algorithm 2 on p. 10). Passive beamforming relaxes the discrete states and runs Adam on each instance (p. 10: "We solve P(A-3) by utilizing Adam optimizer [39] in PyTorch"). The simulation baselines Random, Best Sounding, Group-Opt and Phased Array (p. 10-11) are all non-learned, and the text never says which approximator feeds the estimator in the simulation. If the reviewer counts the DNN surrogate as a learned component, the alternative reason is function (RIS element response modelling, none of the seven areas), so the work stays excluded either way.
